controls.note: Deliberately wrong expectation. The native output is a no-match; it MUST serialize as unknown (INV-005) and this control MUST therefore FAIL. If it ever passes, our reporter normalized unknown->allow and the run is broken.
controls.purpose: Serialization guard: a no-match case with an allow expectation must FAIL; a pass means unknown was normalized to allow (INV-005 violation).

controls.note: Deliberately wrong expectation for the INV-004 case. Actual must be unknown with layer attribution; the control must FAIL. A pass would mean wrapped no-match forms are being reported as decisions.
controls.purpose: INV-004 guard: a wrapped-form no-match with an allow expectation must FAIL; a pass means wrapped forms are reported as decided.

controls.note: Deliberately wrong expectation for a positive control. Actual is allow; the control must FAIL. A pass would mean the oracle path is not actually consulting the native checker.
controls.purpose: Oracle-integrity guard: a deliberately inverted positive control must FAIL; a pass means results are not coming from the native oracle.

controls.note: Deliberately wrong expectation for a negative control. Actual is forbidden; the control must FAIL. A pass would mean the forbidden decision is not being observed.
controls.purpose: Decision-observation guard: a deliberately inverted negative control must FAIL; a pass means the native decision is being misread.

semantics: Each control carries a deliberately WRONG expectation. Run through the same oracle path as the corpus: actual decisions come from 'codex execpolicy check' and serialize under INV-005. A control is HEALTHY only when its verdict is 'fail' (the harness correctly rejected the wrong expectation). If any control's verdict is 'pass', the run is BROKEN and must be reported as such (scientific review addendum, §e: a run that passes its negative controls is a broken run).
